Anya (Partner Success): Quick heads-up — AtlasEdge joint POC kickoff moved to Mon 9am PT. They want a small shared runbook, pricing callouts for burst vs reserved, and answers to their security questionnaire. Can we triage? :calendar:
Matt R. (SE): On it. What QPS/latency targets are they expecting? Need that to size Dedicated vs hosted fallback.
Samir (AtlasEdge): Hi all — aiming for steady-state 50 QPS with 2x burst spikes. P95 latency target ~150ms for generation endpoint. Data will be customer support transcripts (PII redaction planned on our side).
Sunil (Eng-ML): 50 QPS steady with 2x burst is doable with pooling + batching. Recommend dynamic batching + prefix KV cache. For quant: try int8 per our recommendation; saves ~2x memory.
Judy (Security): Two quick asks from the questionnaire: 1) SSO/SAML integration type? 2) KMS for encryption at rest — do they need HSM-backed keys? Also data residency zone?
Samir (AtlasEdge): SSO: SAML 2.0 with IdP metadata. KMS: customer might require HSM for keys containing customer-provided secrets. Data residency: EU only for a subset of tenants.
Anya (Partner Success): Noted. @Elaine can you surface commercial options for EU-only tenancy + HSM? Also we should prepare a prioritized blocker list for Mon.
Elaine (Sales Ops): I'll pull numbers. Two paths: (A) Hosted multi-tenant with EU region + add-on HSM (higher per-token); (B) Dedicated EU pool + annual commit (discounted). Need estimated tokens/day from Samir to calc.
Samir (AtlasEdge): Rough estimate: 8M tokens/day during steady state, peaks ~16M on promos.
Matt R. (SE): With those token volumes, Dedicated rent looks cheaper. I'll draft a quick cost sketch. Also, network: do they want VPC peering or private link?
Samir (AtlasEdge): Prefer VPC peering for direct traffic and lower egress.
Matt R. (SE): OK. Minimal VPC peering checklist:
```
- Customer VPC CIDR
- Allowed ports: 443 (TLS), 22 (support only, optional)
- NACLs: allow established flows
- Route table entry to our peering connection
- MTU 1500
```
Sunil (Eng-ML): For model rollout plan: canary at 5% traffic, auto-fallback to baseline model on degradation, and telemetry sampling at 10% for full traces to limit cost.
Anya (Partner Success): Good. For the runbook — let's include: contact matrix, on-call for SE/infra, SLA escalation, canary checklist, rollback steps, and telemetry links.
partners-bot: POC template: https://redwood.internal/poc-templates/partner-runbook (pre-filled fields: timeline, entitlements, telemetry)
Judy (Security): Also need an export of our pen-test summary and SOC2 AICPA PDF to give them. I'll attach on Monday.
Elaine (Sales Ops): For pricing, two quick numbers (estim): Hosted EU + HSM: $0.045/token equivalent; Dedicated EU 3-node pool w/commit: $XXk/mo (I'll confirm). Will follow up.
Matt R. (SE): Action items: 1) I'll produce an infra sketch + VPC peering snippet. 2) Sunil will provide quantization/throughput profile. 3) Judy will prep security docs. 4) Elaine will email pricing options. 5) Anya to schedule Mon 9am kickoff invite and attach runbook draft. :+1:
Samir (AtlasEdge): Thanks — can we also get a telemetry spec: retention, sampling, PII filtering rules? Their ops team asked.
Sunil (Eng-ML): Telemetry spec: store aggregated metrics 90d, traces 14d by default. Sampling: 10% full traces, 100% aggregated metrics. We scrub PII by default before logging; add explicit fields to whitelist if needed.
Anya (Partner Success): I'll add telemetry spec section to runbook and include the SAML metadata upload step. Meeting invite out in 10m.
Matt R. (SE): One more: recommend enabling automatic fallback to a smaller, cheaper model variant when burst capacity saturates (preserves availability). I'll add that to the rollout doc.
Samir (AtlasEdge): Sounds good. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :rocket:
Anya (Partner Success): Final note — please ping this thread with any docs before the call so I can attach. Cheers! :coffee:
